html:
Nepal is a mountain country in the Himalayas, between Tibet and the plains of India. The map shows it from 1200 to 2010, under very different rulers. Lumbini, in its southern lowlands, is the birthplace of the Buddha.

Main periods:

  • From about 1200 the Malla kings ruled the Kathmandu valley, home of the Newar people, with their pagoda temples and trade with Tibet. In the late 1400s the valley split into three kingdoms: Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur.
  • In 1768 and 1769 Prithvi Narayan Shah, king of the hill state of Gorkha, conquered the valley and founded modern Nepal. His Shah dynasty reigned until 2008.
  • Nepal kept expanding until it lost a war with China in 1792 and the Anglo Nepalese War of 1814 to 1816. Since then Britain, and later India, has recruited Nepali Gurkha soldiers.
  • In 1846 Jung Bahadur took power as prime minister. His Rana family ruled until 1951, kept the kings as figureheads and closed the country to outsiders.

The 1934 earthquake destroyed much of the valley. After Nepal opened, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay climbed Everest from its side in 1953. A Maoist insurgency, the Nepalese Civil War of 1996 to 2006, ended with the abolition of the monarchy in 2008. Nepal is now a federal republic.
sum: Nepal is a mountain country in the Himalayas, between Tibet and the plains of India. The map shows it from 1200 to 2010, under very different rulers. Lumbini, in its southern lowlands, is the birthplace of the Buddha.
